feedback.problem: The coefficient of ${y}^{6}{z}^{3}$ in the expansion of $(y+3z)^{9}$ is
feedback.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have
 

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\frac{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\frac{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\frac{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+…+(\frac{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

In the case of ${(y+3z)}^{9},$ we have $a=y,$ $b=3z,$ and $n=9.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{(y+3z)}^{9}=(\frac{9}{0}){y}^{9}(3z)^{0}+(\frac{9}{1}){y}^{9-1}(3z)^{1}+(\frac{9}{2}){y}^{9-2}(3z)^{2}+⋯+(\frac{9}{9}){y}^{9-9}(3z)^{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the ${y}^{6}{z}^{3}$ term must be

$$
(\frac{9}{3}){y}^{9-3}(3z)^{3}.
$$

Simplifying this term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{9}{3}){y}^{9-3}(3z)^{3} & =84{y}^{6}\cdot {3}^{3}{z}^{3} \\  & =84{y}^{6}\cdot 27{z}^{3} \\  & =2\,268{y}^{6}{z}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${y}^{6}{z}^{3}$ is $2\,268.$
